regions.label: Figure 5.5
regions.summary: Stacked bars compare reported reasons for not using the internet across 22 countries and the total; digital literacy is the largest reason overall (69%).
regions.details: The chart title is “In low- and middle-income countries, nearly 70 percent of those who do not use the internet are held back by deficiencies in digital literacy.” Vertical axis: “Share of respondents (%)”, 0–100, in 10-point increments. Each bar is a 100% stacked bar. Legend, bottom to top colors: Digital literacy (orange), Affordability (green), Relevance (blue), Other (gold). Horizontal categories, left to right: Nepal, Colombia, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Lesotho, Senegal, Peru, Guatemala, Cambodia, Paraguay, Nigeria, Ghana, Ecuador, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Argentina, Uganda, Mozambique, Tanzania, Rwanda, South Africa, Total. Approximate segment readings from the bars (digital literacy / affordability / relevance / other, percent): Nepal 77/10/11/2; Colombia 73/13/9/5; India 73/13/12/2; Bangladesh 72/12/26/0; Pakistan 71/20/7/2; Lesotho 67/13/14/6; Senegal 64/16/10/10; Peru 63/12/6/19; Guatemala 62/13/16/9; Cambodia 61/26/9/4; Paraguay 59/21/19/1; Nigeria 56/24/12/8; Ghana 55/26/11/8; Ecuador 50/20/16/14; Sri Lanka 46/14/34/6; Kenya 37/29/27/7; Argentina 34/18/38/10; Uganda 23/56/15/6; Mozambique 14/76/4/6; Tanzania 13/66/15/6; Rwanda 11/76/4/9; South Africa 9/52/16/23; Total 69/15/12/4. Source: Chen 2021; data URL printed as http://bit.do/WDR2021-Fig-5_5. Note: respondents had access to internet service. Digital literacy responses included “Do not know what internet is” and “Do not know how to use internet”; affordability included “No access device” and “Too expensive”; relevance included “No interest/not useful” and “No relevant content in local language.”
regions.limitations: Country segment values are approximate visual readings from the stacked bars; the chart does not print numeric labels on individual segments. Total values are also supported by the accompanying text for the first three categories (69%, 15%, 12%); Other is approximately 4%.
